newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on institutional buying.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up on Friday on institutional buying of companies which have a heavy weighting in the index, including Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development, brokers said.
The B index rose 1.140 points or 1.31 percent to 88.098 on volume of 37.975 million shares worth $22.988 million.
Brokers said institutions were seen supporting Pudong shares but follow-up buying was limited, indicating further sharp gains will be difficult to achieve.
"Some institutions lifted the prices of shares in which they hold large positions, but follow-up buying was not active with most investors cautious," one broker said.
"The market needs a correction in the short term though some individual stocks may buck the trend," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 16 up, one flat and 25 down.
Shanghai Lujiazui was the most actively traded and became the star on institutional window-dressing buying, jumping $0.092 or 7.30 percent to $1.352 on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Another Pudong share, Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development, followed on the same factors, ending up $0.050 or 7.14 percent to $0.750 on volume of 1.8 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index tumbled late in the session on institutional unwinding selling, triggered by talk that Beijing plans to introduce new measures to cool down the market, brokers said.
The index slipped 16.925 points or 1.17 percent to 1,426.972 points on volume of 973.1 million shares worth 13.7 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index edged up 1.617 points or 0.04 percent to 3,793.814 points.
Shanghai Jiabao Industry & Commerce Co was the biggest loser on poor annual results, plunging 1.33 yuan or 9.98 percent to 11.99 yuan on volume of 2.9 million shares.
